```{r setup,include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE)
library(tidyverse)
```

### My choices

* Gene: GNLY
* Continuous covariate: mat_vitD (vitamin D, ng/mL)
* Categorical covariate 1: mat_BMI (BMI group, derived from a continuous variable)
* Categorical covariate 2: preg_preeclampsia (Normal vs. Preeclampsia)

### Step 1. Load the raw data

```{r load}
#read.csv with row.names = 1 uses the first column (probe IDs) as row names
covar <- read.csv(file = 'GSE85307_covar-1.csv')
geneNames <- read.csv(file = 'GSE85307_geneNames.csv')
expr <- read.csv(file = 'GSE85307_geneExpression.csv', row.names = 1)

# The first column name of the covariate file can come in with a hidden extra
# character (BOM), so we rename it ourselves
colnames(covar)[1] <- 'subjectID'

# Look at the the structure
str(covar)
dim(expr)
head(geneNames)
```

### Step 2. Clean the covariates

Every covariate value is stored as text with a label, like "age_year: xxx". I
remove everything up to and including ":" and then fix the data types.

```{r clean}
# Loop through columns 3 to 10 (all covariates; columns 1-2 are the IDs)
# '.*: ' means "any characters followed by a colon and a space"
for(i in colnames(covar)[3:10]){
  covar[,i] <- sub(pattern = '.*: ',replacement = '', x = covar[,i])
}
head(covar)

# Numeric variables
covar$mat_age_yrs <- as.numeric(covar$mat_age_yrs)
covar$delivery_gestAge_wks <- as.numeric(covar$delivery_gestAge_wks)
covar$sampleCollection_gestAge_wks <- as.numeric(covar$sampleCollection_gestAge_wks)
covar$mat_BMI <- as.numeric(covar$mat_BMI)
covar$mat_vitD <- as.numeric(covar$mat_vitD)

# Categorical variables
covar$preg_preeclampsia <- factor(covar$preg_preeclampsia,
                                  levels = c('Normal','Preeclampsia'))
covar$mat_asthma <- factor(ifelse(covar$mat_asthma=='1','Asthma','Healthy'))

# Check that the types and values look right
str(covar)
summary(covar)
```
### Step 3. Derive a categorical variable from a continuous one

```{r derive}
# BMI groups: <25, 25-30, >=30
# Only 5 women have the BMI < 18.5, too few for their own group, so they are 
# combined with the "<25" group
covar$bmi_group <- cut(covar$mat_BMI,
                       breaks = c(0,25,30,Inf),
                       labels = c('<25','25-30','>=30'))

# Check the sample sizes
table(covar$bmi_group)

```

### Step 4. Find my gene and match it to the covariates

The expression columns are in a different order than the rows of the covriate file,
so I cannot just paste them together. I sort both by sample ID and then check that 
they line up.

```{r match}
geneOfInterest <- 'GNLY'
# Gene name -> probe ID (the row names of expr are the probe IDs, stored as text)
probeID <- geneNames[which(geneNames$GENE==geneOfInterest),'PROBEID']
probeID <- as.character(probeID)

# Make sure there is exactly one probe and that it is in the expression data
length(probeID)
probeID %in% rownames(expr)

# Transpose so samples are rows and pull out the gene's column
exprT <- t(expr)
geneVec <- exprT[,probeID]

# Sort both the covariates and the gene values by sampleID
covar <- covar[order(covar$geoID),]
geneVec <- geneVec[order(names(geneVec))]

# Check every sample must line up(all True)
table(covar$geoID==names(geneVec))

# Only add the gene to the data frame
covar$Expression <- as.numeric(geneVec)
plotData <- covar

# Spot check one sample against the raw expression table (should be TRUE)
expr[probeID,plotData$geoID[1]] == plotData$Expression[1]

# Check the sample sizes per group
table(plotData$bmi_group,plotData$preg_preeclampsia)
```
### Plot 1. Histogram of gene expression

```{r histogram}
ggplot(plotData,aes(x=Expression)) +
  geom_histogram(bins=20,fill='darkgreen',color='white')+
  labs(title = paste('Distribution of',geneOfInterest,'Expression'),
    x=paste(geneOfInterest,'Expression'),
       y='Number of Samples')+
  theme_classic(base_size = 14)
ggsave('submission1_histogram.png')
```
### Plot 2. Continuous covariate vs. gene expression (scatter plot)

```{r scatter}
ggplot(plotData,aes(x=mat_vitD,y=Expression))+
  geom_point(size = 2)+
  geom_smooth(method = lm, color = 'darkgreen')+
  ggpubr::stat_cor(method = 'pearson',
                   label.x = 45,
                   label.y = 11.2,
                   p.accuracy = 0.001)+
  # label.x / label.y move the label to the empty upper-right corner;
  # p.accuracy = 0.001 stops it from printing a long p-value
  labs(title = paste(geneOfInterest,'Expression vs. Maternal Vitamin D'),
    x='Maternal Vitamin D (ng/mL)',
       y=paste(geneOfInterest,'Expression'))+
  theme_classic(base_size = 14)
  
ggsave('submission1_scatter.png')

```
### Plot 3. Boxplot by both categorical variables

```{r boxplot}
# Define the color palette
colorPalette <- c('grey50','darkgreen')

ggplot(plotData,aes(x=bmi_group,y=Expression,fill=preg_preeclampsia))+
  geom_boxplot(outlier.shape = NA)+
  # outlier.shape = NA hides the boxplot's own outlier dots, because every
  # sample is drawn as a point below 
  geom_point(aes(group=preg_preeclampsia),
             position = position_jitterdodge(jitter.width = 0.15),
             size = 1.5)+
  # Individual samples on top of the boxes. It spreads points inside each box
  # so they do not overlap.
  scale_fill_manual(values = colorPalette)+
  labs(title = paste(geneOfInterest,
                     'Expression by BMI Group and Pregnancy Condition'),
    x='BMI Group(kg/m^2)',
       y=paste(geneOfInterest,'Expression'),
       fill='Pregnancy Condition')+
  theme_classic(base_size = 14)+
  theme(legend.position = 'top')
ggsave('submission1_boxplot.png')
```
